source_text: Quoniam tamen dominus prospector humanarum neces- 10 sitatum seorsum post traditam orandi disciplinam, petite, inquit, et accipietis, et sunt, quae petantur pro circumstantia cuiusque, praemissa legitima et ordinaria oratione quasi fundamento, accedentium ius est desideriorum superstruendi extrinsecus petitiones, cum memoria tamen praeceptorum.
orientation: Tertullian is explaining how Christians may add their own particular requests to the fixed and ordinary prayer that Christ taught.
pass_a_gloss: Since nevertheless the Lord, the provider of human necessities, separately after the teaching of praying had been handed over, said, 'Ask, and you will receive,' and there are things which may be asked for according to each person's circumstance, after the lawful and ordinary prayer has been sent ahead as a foundation, it is the right of those approaching to build upon it from outside their own petitions of desires, with remembrance nevertheless of the precepts.

choices.why: Keeps the noun 'prospector' as an agent noun, matching Tertullian's title for the Lord as one who looks after human needs.
rejected: the one who foresees human needs

choices.why: Uses the glossary rendering 'teaching' for disciplina and keeps the gerund 'orandi' as 'of praying' to preserve the action.

choices.term: praemissa legitima et ordinaria oratione quasi fundamento
choices.english: after the lawful and ordinary prayer has been sent ahead as a foundation
choices.why: Renders the ablative absolute literally, keeping 'sent ahead' for praemissa and 'as a foundation' for quasi fundamento.
rejected: with the lawful and ordinary prayer laid down as a foundation
once the established and regular prayer has been offered as a base

choices.term: accedentium ius est desideriorum superstruendi extrinsecus petitiones
choices.english: it is the right of those approaching to build upon it from outside their own petitions of desires
choices.why: Preserves the genitive 'accedentium' as 'of those approaching' and the gerundive 'superstruendi' as 'of building upon', keeping the legal metaphor of 'ius' as 'right'.
rejected: those who approach have the right to add their own requests
it is permitted for those who come to pile on additional petitions

choices.english: with remembrance nevertheless of the precepts
choices.why: Keeps the concessive 'tamen' as 'nevertheless' and the noun 'memoria' as 'remembrance' to match the following section's opening.
rejected: provided the precepts are kept in mind

pass_b_english: Yet since the Lord looks after human needs, he said separately, after handing over the teaching of praying, “Ask, and you will receive” (Matthew 7:7). There are things to be asked for according to each person's circumstances. Once the lawful and ordinary prayer has been placed first as a foundation, those who approach have the right to build their own petitions of desires upon it from outside—provided they still remember the precepts.
